# Proposal: Govern on every closing reference, sourced from the platform

Change: issue-545-closing-reference-coverage
File: openspec/changes/issue-545-closing-reference-coverage/proposal.md
Worktree: /home/gandalf/IA/brain-issue-545 (branch fix/issue-545-fixgovernance-the-closing-reference-pars)

## Intent

`extractIssueNumber` (brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs:233) returns the FIRST CLOSING_RE match. Measured over the 100 most recently merged PRs vs GitHub's own `closingIssuesReferences`:

| Signal | Count |
|---|---|
| Bodies with >1 match | 30 |
| brain's pick NOT in GitHub's closing set (the ticket's stated defect) | 0 |
| brain sees a ref, GitHub sees none | 3 (#502/#503/#504 -> #473) |
| GitHub closes >1 issue while brain verifies 1 | 7 |

RE-FRAME (stated honestly, not quietly): the ticket says brain "picks the wrong one". That has NEVER fired — it is real but LATENT. The defect that HAS fired is UNDER-COVERAGE: brain verifies one of several closing targets, 7 times in 100.

The seven: #678 (verifies 675 / closes 674,675), #656 (655 / 628,655), #592 (477 / 477,591), #534 (479 / 475,479), #524 (386 / 386,387,388), #512 (511 / 499,511), #482 (466 / 466,474).

CONFIRMED LIVE VIOLATION: PR #592 declared `Closes #477` (approved, verified) and `Closes #591`. GitHub closed both. #591 carried type:bug and never status:approved; closed 2026-08-13T16:23:02Z, 2s after merge. Invariant 1 satisfied in the letter, violated in the effect.

## Scope

In scope: resolve a closing-reference SET not a single number and verify EVERY member is approved; source that set from the platform via a new VCS verb with regex fallback; apply to BOTH consumers (issue-link and memory-gate); name/handle the mirror defect.
Out of scope: CLOSING_RE/CHAIN_RE vocabulary and default-branch conditionality; actor-check.mjs and brain-metrics.mjs copies of extractIssueNumber (follow-up); retroactive remediation of #591 (recommended, not executed).

## Capabilities

New: `vcs-closing-refs-contract` — cross-provider contract for the closing-references verb (GitHub closingIssuesReferences, GitLab closes_issues), incl. uncomputable-vs-empty discipline.
Modified: `governance-v3` (REQ-L3-4, memory-gate issue-scoping over a set); `governance` (REQ-S2-1, issue-link verifies every closing target).

## Approach — five decisions

DECISION 1 — the rule: VERIFY ALL.
- Verify every target, all must be approved -> CHOSEN. Zero false refusals: all 7 multi-target PRs were legitimate; only #592 would have blocked, correctly.
- Verify first, REFUSE on >1 distinct target -> REJECTED. Would have blocked 10 of the last 100 legitimate PRs; the operator's only recourse is splitting a merged intent or an exception label. Not acceptable.
- Keep first-match, file the rest -> REJECTED. Leaves the invariant advisory.

DECISION 2 (LOAD-BEARING) — source of the set: ASK THE PLATFORM.
Regex-parity is cheaper but only ever APPROXIMATES the field GitHub acts on; it cannot close the 3 GitHub-sees-none cases and re-opens drift on every keyword edge. Cost is LOWER than the ticket assumed: no raw GraphQL client needed — `gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences` rides the existing gh spawn path in providers/github.mjs; `GET projects/:id/merge_requests/:iid/closes_issues` rides gitlab.mjs's existing gitlabApiFetch path. `ctx.prNumber` is ALREADY in ci-context.mjs. Real cost: one port verb (doc table + cli.mjs VERBS + both providers + contract test + fixtures, per verb-contract-drift-guard.test.mjs) and one network call in a gate that already makes one (issueView).
Fail-closed: verb uncomputable -> `uncomputable: true`, never a silent fallback to a regex-only pass.

DECISION 3 — the 3 mirror cases (#502/#503/#504 -> #473). Chained slice PRs whose base was not the default branch; the PR template accepts `Part of #N` off-default. GitHub does not act on their keywords, so brain governs a reference the platform will IGNORE. Benign (over-governs) but NAMED: on a non-default target the platform set is empty by design, so brain keeps regex-derived resolution there. The platform set is authoritative only where the platform acts — the default branch.

DECISION 4 — memory-gate. Shares extractIssueNumber. With >1 issue, memoryRetrieval must accept a record scoped to ANY target (permissive OR), matching its existing permissive posture (REQ-L3-4 already degrades rather than fails closed). Tightening to "one record per issue" is a separate policy change, deliberately NOT made here.

DECISION 5 — the retro (MAINTAINER'S CALL, recommended not decided). #591 is closed and unapproved today. Recommendation: label it status:approved retroactively with a comment citing PR #592, or record a governance exception. Re-opening buys nothing — the work shipped.

## Affected areas
- brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs — extractIssueNumber becomes set-returning; runIssueLinkCheck and runMemoryGateCheck loop
- brain/scripts/vcs/providers/github.mjs, providers/gitlab.mjs — new verb
- brain/scripts/vcs/cli.mjs + brain/core/methodology/vcs-contract.md — verb registration (drift guard reconciles doc table, VERBS, and provider exports)
- brain/scripts/vcs/providers/vcs.contract.test.mjs + fixtures — contract coverage
- brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-ref-patterns.mjs — UNCHANGED (one parser stays one parser)

## Risks
- New network call flakes -> gate blocks (Med): reuse issueView's uncomputable/fail-closed discipline with a distinct self-diagnostic reason.
- GitLab closes_issues payload shape differs from assumed (Med): verify in design; derived fixtures + contract test before wiring.
- Newly-strict gate blocks in-flight PRs (Low): 0 of last 100 would fail except the true violation.
- Partial verb registration fails the drift guard (Low): register doc + VERBS + both providers in one commit.

## Rollback
Single revert of the run-check.mjs set-resolution commit restores first-match behavior; the new verb is additive and inert without its caller. No data migration, no persisted state.

## Dependencies
- `gh` CLI support for the `closingIssuesReferences` JSON field on the CI runner's version — VERIFY IN DESIGN.
- GitLab `closes_issues` endpoint shape — VERIFY IN DESIGN.

## Success criteria
- [ ] A PR body closing an approved AND an unapproved issue FAILS issue-link.
- [ ] Replaying the 7 multi-target PRs: all pass except #592, which fails on #591.
- [ ] Replaying #502/#503/#504: still resolve #473, no regression off the default branch.
- [ ] Platform-verb failure yields uncomputable: true, never a silent pass.
- [ ] memory-gate passes when a record is scoped to any closing target.
- [ ] verb-contract-drift-guard green; contract test covers both providers.
